summary: Ran a declaration-keyword grep over all 47 changed/added files. Two files matched zero declarations: BtcVerified.lean and Tests.lean, both read in full -- each is a bare list of `import ...` lines with no open/notation/alias/executable commands, so both are pure import aggregators retained under FILTER-007 as navigation modules. All other files carry real Lean content: the BtcVerified/ tree is the Bitcoin consensus/serialization formalization (Block, Chainstate, Consensus, Crypto, Ext, Packed, Script, Serialize, Transaction), and Tests/ holds golden vectors, block fixtures, an axiom audit, and the module-discipline auditor and its fixtures, matching the prior review's own description. Two files, BenchMain.lean and ModuleAuditMain.lean, were read in full: each declares exactly one `def main`/`unsafe def main` IO driver that only sequences calls into logic fully defined and retained elsewhere (BenchMain.lean calls Tests.BlockFixtures.fetchFixture and Tests.Bench.benchBlock, both retained in Tests/Bench.lean; ModuleAuditMain.lean calls ModuleAudit.run ModuleAudit.btcVerifiedPolicy, retained and fully defined in ModuleAudit.lean, 40 declarations) and returns an IO exit code -- the same content pattern the prior review (RRV-69bcd32b76e6-r1) already excluded for TestsMain.lean in this same source, which remains excluded unchanged. Both are excluded on that established precedent; the logic they invoke stays fully searchable under its own declaring file.
